problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,x,\,3x+y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined in Cartesian coordinates as $z=-1$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $1\le y\le 2.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the *downward*-pointing unit normal vector $n.$

feedback.problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨y,\,z,\,2x⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined in Cartesian coordinates as $z=2$ for $0\le x\le 3$ and $0\le y\le 2.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the upward-pointing unit normal vector $n.$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

For the surface $z=2$ for $0\le x\le 3$ and $0\le y\le 2,$ the upward-pointing unit normal vector is

$$
n=⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩.
$$

Using the fact that $z=2$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨y,\,z,\,2x⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨y,\,2,\,2x⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}2x\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}2x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}2x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}y{\int }_{0}^{3}2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot {[{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =18\end{aligned}
$$
